articles.title: Man charged with mailing threatening letters to Illinois lawmakers
articles.description: An Illinois man has been charged with mailing four letters containing a white granular substance to members of Congress in the Chicago area.

articles.title: Feds say Quincy man mailed letters containing white powder to members of Illinois congressional delegation
articles.description: The letters were postmarked in Springfield on Oct. 19 and contained handwritten messages, including “HA HA” and “HAH enjoy the gift,” according to an FBI affidavit.

articles.title: Illinois man with lengthy criminal history arrested in white-powder threats to members of Congress
articles.description: Matthew Unglesbee is facing his first federal charge after the FBI said he admitted sending threatening envelopes to four Illinois members of Congress.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: FBI Says Man Sent Anthrax-Style Scare Letters to Four Members of Congress — As Agents Uncover Fifth Envelope
articles.description: Illinois man Matthew Unglesbee faces federal charges after allegedly mailing white powder and chilling messages to four members of Congress.

articles.title: Illinois Man Accused Of Mailing White Powder To Members Of Congress
articles.description: Matthew Ungelsbee, 37, is charged with sending threatening letters to members of Congress containing a white powder, including one with a note reading “HAH enjoy the gift.”.

articles.title: Illinois Man Charged With Mailing White Powder to Four Members of Congress
articles.description: The suspect said the substance was actually salt but that it “kind of looks like” anthrax.

articles.title: Illinois man charged with sending 'threatening notes' and mailing 'white powder letters' to Congress members
articles.description: An Illinois man has been charged with mailing four threatening letters containing a white granular substance to members of Congress, prompting an FBI investigation
